glosses: спорт. в боксе и других видах ударных единоборств — приводить (привести) в состояние нокаута

examples.text: В шестидесятом году Мохаммед Али нокаутировал Петшиковского.

glosses: перен. неприятно поражать (поразить), сильно огорчать (огорчить), приводить (привести) в состояние беспомощности
To strike or bump (someone or something) out.

examples.text: I accidentally knocked out the glass in my picture frame.

glosses: To render unconscious, as by a blow to the head.

examples.text: The boxer knocked out his opponent in the third round.

In the autumn there was a row at some cement works about the unskilled labour men. A union had just been started for them and all but a few joined. One of these blacklegs was laid for by a picket and knocked out of time.
The allergy pill knocked him out for a good three hours.
That's a put-you-straight-to-sleep book if there ever was one, and I knocked right out after two paragraphs.
Running errands all day really knocked him out.

glosses: To cause a mechanism to become non-functional by damaging or destroying it.

examples.text: The antitank gun knocked out the enemy tank.

glosses: To eliminate from a contest or similar.

examples.text: As they were approaching bankruptcy from being knocked out of the calculator market, they began development on the first commercially available microcomputer, the Altair.
Tottenham were knocked out of the Europa League, despite a comfortable victory over Shamrock Rovers in Dublin.
The prisoner knocked out a message on the wall for the prisoner in the adjoining cell.

glosses: To complete, especially in haste; knock off.

examples.text: They knocked out the entire project in one night.

glosses: To lose the scent of hounds in fox-hunting.
To leave college after hours—after half-past ten at night when the doors have been locked.

examples.text: "Hullo!" he said, getting up; "time for me to knock out, or old Copas will be in bed. […]"

glosses: To obtain or earn (something, often money or food).
En el boxeo, lucha y otros deportes de combate, victoria por pérdida de conocimiento (nocaut) del adversario.

examples.text: „Der Halbschwergewichtsweltmeister hatte die Verletzung bereits in der vierten Runde erlitten, boxte aber noch weitere fünf Runden und knockte Harmon mit einer Schlagserie in der neunten Runde aus.“
Resi knockt ihren Bruder regelmäßig beim Memory aus.
Er hat alle Gegner beim Gesangswettbewerb ausgeknockt.

Vu cette cruelle maladie qui atteint de nombreux boxeurs, Thérèse traduit en mots les pensées de son mari, ce héros dans la défaite qui, en 1958, a failli knockouter Archie Moore, le champion mondial.

À 7 heures le matin, du côté de Buzenval, des Maraîchers, “un coup d’Air-Wick aurait pas été d’trop pour knockouter les r’lents de galtouze, de claquos, d’oignon et d’panard qui emboucanaient l’tube”.
